D16ADA.title: Ex-MEDD: An Explainable Multimodal Ensemble Framework for Deepfake Detection
D16ADA.description: Synthetic media generated through deepfake techniques is increasingly being used to spread misinformation, manipulate public opinion, and fabricate evidence. The core limitation of most current detectors is that they look at only one signal - image, audio, or video - and are built around a single model, which makes them easy to fool when the forgery is more layered. This paper introduces Ex-MEDD (Explainable Multimodal Ensemble for Deepfake Detection), a framework we built to tackle this problem by analysing all three modalities together through a 16-model ensemble, where each model brings a different perspective on what a fake looks like. We train the system on the InDeepFake dataset, which covers six types of manipulation including face-swap and voice-synced lip-sync methods, and test generalization on FaceForensics++ and FakeAVCeleb. Rather than training everything at once, we use a three-stage approach: first each model learns on its own, then we train only the combination layer, and finally we fine-tune the full system together at a reduced learning rate. This prevents stronger models from drowning out weaker ones. Our results show that the ensemble outperforms every individual model across all three modalities and holds up well on datasets it was not trained on. Beyond detection accuracy, we address a practical gap that most systems ignore: explainability. Each prediction comes with visual maps and frame-level traces that show what the model actually reacted to, which matters in real-world use cases like journalism verification or legal review.

D16ADA.title: Tinyflamingo- SLM for medical scan analysis
D16ADA.description: The MedFlamingo project addresses the critical challenge of hallucinations and brittle evaluation metrics in medical vision-language models.This framework enables sophisticated medical reasoning on resource-constrained hardware.. The core innovation is a Composite Reward Function integrated into a Group-Based Reinforcement Learning pipeline, utilizing algorithms like GRPO and DAPO to stabilize optimization in the subjective medical domain. This multi-signal reward includes an LLM-Based Accuracy signal judged by a Qwen3-4B model ,a medical-specific Semantic Reward and a mandatory Modality Grounding signal to ensure scan types like MRI or X-ray are explicitly identified before reasoning.To anchor this reinforcement learning loop in clinical truth, MedGemma-4B serves as the Context Model, providing high-quality ground-truth references for the judge model to evaluate against. This dual-model framework enforces structural integrity through a standardized output format featuring interpretable <think> reasoning traces and a concise <answer>.

D16ADA.title: Government Grievance Redressal using SLM
D16ADA.description:
Government grievance redressal systems handle millions of citizen complaints annually, yet they often suffer from delayed processing, misclassification, and inefficient routing across departments. Existing platforms largely depend on manual intervention or rule-based automation, limiting scalability and
responsiveness. This paper proposes an intelligent grievance redressal framework leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) based multi-agent architecture powered by Small Language Models (specifically Llama-3-8B) to enable scalable, policyaware governance automation. The proposed system employs specialized AI agents for grievance intake, semantic classification, sentiment analysis, similarity matching with historical cases, policy retrieval, and decision support. A vector database stores grievance embeddings and government policies, enabling contextaware responses without requiring model retraining. The use of parameter-efficient SLMs (8 billion parameters) significantly
reduces deployment costs while maintaining operational effectiveness for resource-constrained government environments. The implementation demonstrates 100% system reliability through fault-tolerant design, reducing processing time from 15-30 minutes to 2-3 minutes per complaint. The results indicate that the proposed RAG-based multi-agent approach improves transparency, responsiveness, and operational efficiency, making it suitable for large-scale deployment in government environments.

D16ADA.title: Personalized RAG-based AI Research Assistant
D16ADA.description: Researchq is a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) based research assistant designed to simplify querying and understanding of academic PDFs. It addresses the challenge of extracting relevant information from large research documents by combining semantic search with modern large language models.The system processes PDFs by splitting them into smaller chunks and converting them into embeddings using transformer-based models. These embeddings are stored in a FAISS vector database, enabling efficient similarity-based retrieval. When a user submits a query, the system retrieves the most relevant document segments and uses a Gemini-based language model to generate accurate, context-aware responses grounded in the source material.The application uses Streamlit for an interactive user interface and is fully containerized using Docker, ensuring easy deployment across environments such as Linux and AWS EC2 without manual setup. Its modular architecture allows flexibility for future enhancements like advanced retrieval techniques and multi-vector support.Overall, researchq provides a scalable and efficient solution for research document exploration, improving productivity and enabling faster knowledge discovery.

D16ADA.title:
MOCKMATE.AI
An AI-Powered Interview Companion
D16ADA.description: An intelligent Mock interview platform that combines AI-powered resume optimization with realistic voice-based mock interviews, helping job seekers practice and improve their interview skills in a safe environment. It generates ATS compatibility reports with keyword scores, section-wise analysis, and actionable resume optimization tips to pass initial screenings. It provides performance feedback on technical skills, communication, confidence, and problem-solving with detailed feedback and improvement recommendations.

D16ADA.title: MediSuite AI Agent - Healthcare and Insurance Workflow Automation
D16ADA.description: MediSuite AI Agent is an AI-assisted system for healthcare and insurance workflow automation. It leverages OCR, NLP, and a RAG pipeline to automate ICD-10 and CPT-4 medical coding, generate standardized insurance claim forms and provide transparency dashboards for patients. The system reduces claim rejection rates, minimizes manual errors, improves billing efficiency, and builds trust in healthcare institutions through accurate, transparent, and scalable AI-driven solutions.

D16ADA.title: AI-Assisted Criminal Face Generation using Witness Descriptions
D16ADA.description: The project, "AI-Assisted Criminal Face Generation using Witness Description" is a system that takes a textual description of a criminal's face from a witness and combines it with a sketch. Utilizing a contrastive learning model, it translates these combined inputs into a realistic, high-quality photograph of the criminal. This technology aims to assist law enforcement by providing a more accurate and useful visual representation for identification and apprehension.

D16ADA.title: Admeme:Advertisement through memes using Visual language model
D16ADA.description: Admeme is an autonomous marketing agent designed to bridge the gap between corporate branding and internet culture. It leverages RAG, n8n orchestration, and a Vision-Language (VL) pipeline to automate real-time trend ingestion and viral meme synthesis. The system features a fine-tuned Llama 3.2 11B Vision model that acts as a "Vision Critic," assigning Virality Scores based on cognitive and social metrics. By automating the selection of templates and the generation of sarcastic, relatable captions, it reduces marketing lag and improves cultural relevance through scalable, data-driven AI solutions.

D16ADA.title: Agentify - Agent as a Service Platform
D16ADA.description:
Agentify is an intelligent multi-agent automation platform designed to streamline and enhance digital workflows by integrating artificial intelligence with real-world business operations. The system combines a modern React-based frontend with a robust FastAPI backend, enabling users to interact with multiple AI-powered agents through a unified and intuitive interface. The primary goal of Agentify is to reduce manual effort, improve efficiency, and provide scalable automation solutions across domains such as email marketing, social media management, website generation, and lead acquisition.

The architecture of Agentify is based on a modular, agent-oriented design where each agent is responsible for a specific functionality and operates independently via RESTful API endpoints. This separation of concerns allows for better scalability, maintainability, and flexibility, as new agents or features can be added without affecting existing components. The frontend, built using React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, provides a responsive and user-friendly dashboard, while Axios handles seamless communication with backend services.

At the core of the backend lies FastAPI, which manages routing, agent orchestration, and integration with external services. The Email Automation Agent enables users to generate personalized and context-aware email content using advanced AI models and send emails either individually or in bulk using Gmail SMTP. It also incorporates an automated reply monitoring system using the Gmail API, supported by APScheduler for periodic background polling, ensuring continuous engagement tracking.

The Social Media Agent focuses on content creation and publishing. It generates high-quality text posts and AI-based images using a robust fallback pipeline that includes Pollinations.ai, FLUX.1-schnell, SDXL-Flash, and Gemini Image models. This ensures reliability and availability even if one service fails. Additionally, the agent supports automated posting to platforms such as Twitter and Instagram through APIs and browser automation techniques.

The Website Builder Agent utilizes large language models like Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4o-mini to dynamically generate website structures and content, enabling rapid prototyping and deployment of web pages. The Lead Finder Agent leverages geolocation and mapping services such as Nominatim, Photon, and Overpass APIs to identify businesses based on user queries. It further employs asynchronous web scraping techniques to extract relevant contact information, such as email addresses, from business websites, facilitating efficient lead generation.

Agentify integrates multiple AI models with fallback mechanisms to ensure robustness and uninterrupted service. It also incorporates local storage and caching strategies for managing CSV data, authentication tokens, and session persistence. Background job scheduling using APScheduler enhances automation by handling recurring tasks without user intervention.

In conclusion, Agentify represents a comprehensive and scalable AI-driven automation platform that combines multi-agent architecture, advanced AI model integration, and external API connectivity. It significantly improves productivity and operational efficiency, making it a powerful solution for modern business automation and digital transformation.

D16ADA.title: Eco clean - AI powered social cleanups and community
D16ADA.description:
EcoClean is an AI-powered, community-driven platform designed to modernize environmental cleanup drives in coastal and urban areas. As plastic waste, non-biodegradable materials, and unmanaged litter continue to grow, traditional campaigns struggle with poor coordination, limited transparency, and low volunteer engagement. EcoClean addresses these challenges through a centralized digital system that effectively combines community participation with intelligent automation.
The platform enables users to register, discover nearby cleanup events, and join organized drives with ease. Volunteers upload before-and-after images of cleaned areas, which serve as both proof of participation and impact measurement tools. These images are analyzed using YOLOv8-based AI, which detects and classifies waste types such as plastic, glass, and metal, enabling accurate monitoring and the generation of meaningful environmental insights.
Location-based event discovery via Maps API helps volunteers find the nearest cleanup drive, while waste collection statistics provide a clear picture of total impact achieved. A built-in chatbot guides users on waste segregation, safety instructions, and event-related queries, making the experience more accessible for newcomers and seasoned volunteers alike.
To sustain long-term engagement, EcoClean incorporates a gamification system featuring points, badges, and a leaderboard that recognizes and rewards active contributors. Organizers benefit from automated caption and content generation, simplifying the creation of social media posts and promotional material for upcoming campaigns.
Authenticity is maintained through an image validation and fraud prevention mechanism that verifies uploads using timestamps and event context, ensuring that rewards and impact reports always reflect genuine participation. Additional features including event participation counters, feedback and rating systems, photo galleries, and participation certificate generation make the platform practical and ready for real-world deployment.
Overall, EcoClean demonstrates how AI, location services, and community engagement can transform traditional cleanup drives into organized, transparent, and data-driven environmental initiatives — offering a scalable framework with strong potential for future smart city and sustainability applications.

D16ADA.title: Smart Research Paper Assistant for phd Scholars using Generative AI
D16ADA.description: Doctoral research today faces a growing challenge of information overload, where researchers must continuously search, organize, revisit, and compare large volumes of scholarly literature while maintaining originality in their writing. Although existing academic search engines provide access to published research, they offer limited support for researchers working with personal collections of PDF documents and seeking fast, context- aware assistance tailored to their own libraries. This project presents a Smart Research Paper Assistant de- signed to support researchers throughout the literature review and knowledge management process. The proposed system in- tegrates document ingestion and personal library management with PDF text extraction and preprocessing, transformer-based summarization, embedding-based semantic search using a vector database, related paper recommendation, plagiarism detection, and an early-stage voice-based querying interface. The assistant is built using an Agentic AI framework, in which specialized agents for retrieval, summarization, recommendation, and val- idation collaborate under the control of a centralized backend orchestrator.

D16ADA.title: Sanskriti: Preserving India's dying traditions through AI
D16ADA.description: Sanskriti is an AI-powered platform that preserves India’s fading cultural heritage by processing audio, text, and images into structured, accessible digital content. It uses technologies like speech recognition, NLP, and image enhancement to create an interactive, multilingual cultural archive.

D16ADA.title:
VisioNiX: A Multimodal AI Assistant for Image
Recognition and Conversational Reasoning
D16ADA.description: Multimodal artificial intelligence (MM-AI) represents a paradigm shift in machine comprehension, enabling systems to interpret and reason across integrated visual and textual information. Despite significant advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) and computer vision, current solutions remain fragmented, requiring multiple specialized APIs and lacking unified reasoning capabilities. This paper presents VisioNiX, a novel scalable MM-AI assistant that unifies state-of-the-art computer vision, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and Large Language Models to facilitate sophisticated visual question answering and complex scene analysis. The system employs an innovative multi-agent architecture where specialized deep learning models collaborate in a seamless pipeline: YOLOv8 for object detection achieving 95.4% mAP@50, EasyOCR/TrOCR for robust text extraction, and a LLaVA-based Vision-Language Fusion layer for contextual reasoning achieving 93.1% accuracy on multimodal tasks. Through rigorous evaluation on customcurated datasets containing 1,000+ annotated samples across medical, industrial, and retail domains, VisioNiX demonstrated superior performance compared to traditional unintegrated baselines and commercial black-box solutions. The system supports modular expansion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for knowledge grounding and continuous refinement through Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF), offering significant potential for enterprise deployment in industrial IoT monitoring, automated e-commerce, digital archiving, and assistive technologies

D16ADA.title: Hallucination Detection Using RL and WSD
D16ADA.description:
The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) such as those developed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google has significantly improved the ability of artificial intelligence systems to generate human-like text. However, a critical challenge associated with these models is the phenomenon of hallucination, where the system produces information that appears plausible but is factually incorrect or misleading. This project presents a novel approach for detecting hallucinations in AI-generated responses using a hybrid methodology that combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD).

The proposed system, termed RL-WSD Hallucination Detector, is designed as a full-stack web application that interacts with multiple AI platforms to generate responses and evaluate their factual reliability. The system accepts user queries and forwards them to an AI model such as GPT, Claude, or Gemini. The generated response is then processed through a multi-stage verification pipeline. Initially, the system checks for the presence of the query within a predefined dataset. If the query is found, the response is validated using dataset-based comparison techniques.

To address the limitation of closed-domain systems, the project incorporates an open-domain fallback mechanism using external knowledge retrieval. In cases where the query is not present in the dataset, the system automatically retrieves relevant information from external sources such as Wikipedia. The retrieved content is then compared with the AI-generated response using semantic similarity measures, enabling dynamic validation for unseen queries.

The core innovation of this project lies in the integration of Reinforcement Learning and Word Sense Disambiguation. The WSD module analyzes the contextual meaning of key terms in the AI response using lexical databases and semantic embeddings to detect inconsistencies in word usage. Simultaneously, the RL module assigns rewards or penalties based on factual alignment between the response and verified knowledge. These two components are combined to compute a final hallucination score using a weighted scoring mechanism.

The system classifies responses into three categories: Accurate, Partially Hallucinated, and Hallucinated, along with a confidence score. Additionally, performance evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are implemented to assess the effectiveness of the model.

This project contributes to the growing field of trustworthy AI by providing a scalable and adaptive solution for hallucination detection. By integrating hybrid validation techniques and enabling open-domain query handling, the proposed system enhances the reliability of AI-generated content. The RL-WSD Hallucination Detector can be applied in domains such as education, healthcare, and research, where factual accuracy is critical.

D16ADA.title: AI-Driven Personalized Travel Itinerary Generation System
D16ADA.description:
Group travel planning presents a significant challenge, as travelers within a group often have diverse preferences, varying medical conditions, and different budget expectations. Most existing itinerary planning tools adopt a one-size-fits-all approach, treating all users uniformly and ignoring individual constraints. This limitation makes them inadequate for real-world group travel scenarios, where personalization, safety, and coordination are critical. In this work, we present TripMap, an AI-driven travel planning system designed to address these complexities through a hybrid approach combining rule-based intelligence with lightweight machine learning models.
TripMap introduces a multi-layered architecture that integrates several intelligent components to deliver a personalized and safe travel experience. At its core, the system uses a weighted multi-factor scoring engine to rank attractions based on factors such as fun, comfort, accessibility, and risk. This ensures that suggested itineraries are not only engaging but also suitable for the group’s overall profile. To further enhance safety, the system incorporates a medical and child safety filter that dynamically removes or replaces high-risk activities based on traveler attributes such as age, health conditions, and physical stamina. This is particularly useful for families with children, elderly travelers, or individuals with specific medical concerns.
Another key component of TripMap is its automated group conflict resolution mechanism. In group travel scenarios, conflicting interests are common—for example, some travelers may prefer adventure activities while others may prefer relaxed sightseeing. The system resolves such conflicts by prioritizing group safety and maximizing overall satisfaction through balanced itinerary generation. Additionally, a budget forecasting module predicts realistic travel expenses by analyzing itinerary structure, duration, and group size. This helps users plan within their financial limits while maintaining a practical and enjoyable experience.

To further enhance usability, TripMap integrates a bilingual conversational chatbot powered by a hybrid TinyLLaMA and rule-based architecture. Unlike purely LLM-based systems, which may produce inconsistent or hallucinated outputs, this hybrid approach ensures reliable, context-aware, and controlled responses. The chatbot assists users with queries related to itinerary details, travel tips, safety advice, weather conditions, and cost optimization, providing a seamless and interactive user experience.
In addition to itinerary planning, TripMap extends its functionality by incorporating a basic travel booking module. This feature allows users to explore transportation options such as flights, trains, buses, and car rentals based on their budget and travel preferences. It also provides hotel recommendations tailored to the number of days and budget constraints specified by the user. While the system does not perform direct ticket booking, it simulates realistic options and enables users to make informed decisions regarding travel and accommodation planning. This integration bridges the gap between itinerary generation and actual travel execution, making the system more comprehensive and practical.
The system was evaluated across six key performance metrics. Itinerary generation achieved an average response time of 730 milliseconds across ten different destinations, demonstrating high efficiency suitable for real-time applications. The child safety filtering module achieved 100% accuracy across 20 test scenarios, ensuring reliable risk mitigation. Budget estimation accuracy ranged between 93% and 96%, indicating strong predictive capability. The chatbot achieved 92% accuracy across 50 diverse user queries, reflecting effective conversational performance. The conflict resolution module successfully handled 18 out of 20 group scenarios, and overall user satisfaction was rated at 4.6 out of 5 based on survey feedback.
The results highlight that combining deterministic rule-based systems with lightweight language models offers a robust solution for safety-critical and latency-sensitive applications such as travel planning. Compared to purely LLM-based approaches, this hybrid methodology provides better control, reliability, and domain-specific accuracy. TripMap demonstrates that intelligent integration of multiple AI components can significantly improve the quality, safety, and usability of group travel planning systems, making it a promising solution for real-world deployment.

D16ADA.title: GeoSmartAi : Autonomous Geospatial Analysis via Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Agent
D16ADA.description:
The rapid expansion of geospatial data and the increasing complexity of spatial analysis workflows have created a strong need for intelligent systems that can simplify Geographic Information System (GIS) operations. Traditional GIS tools require significant domain expertise, manual configuration, and knowledge of specialized software such as QGIS, GRASS GIS, and GDAL. Even relatively straightforward spatial decision-making problems, such as identifying suitable locations for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations or analyzing flood-prone areas, often involve multiple complex steps including data collection, preprocessing, spatial transformations, and visualization. These processes are time-consuming, error-prone, and inaccessible to non-experts. Therefore, there is a growing demand for systems that can bridge the gap between natural language understanding and geospatial computation, enabling users to perform complex spatial analysis using simple text-based queries. 

This project presents GeoSmartAI, a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) driven Large Language Model (LLM) framework designed to orchestrate intelligent geoprocessing workflows for complex spatial analysis tasks. The system integrates modern LLMs such as LLaMA-3, Mistral, or similar models with open-source GIS tools and Python-based spatial libraries including GeoPandas, Rasterio, and WhiteboxTools. By leveraging the reasoning capability of LLMs, the system acts as an intelligent GIS assistant capable of interpreting user queries, decomposing them into logical geospatial operations, and generating structured workflows automatically. This approach significantly reduces the technical barrier traditionally associated with GIS analysis and promotes accessibility for researchers, planners, and decision-makers without extensive geospatial expertise. 

The proposed framework utilizes Chain-of-Thought reasoning to ensure transparency and interpretability in decision-making. Instead of producing direct outputs, the model generates intermediate reasoning steps that explain why specific spatial operations are required. Additionally, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is incorporated to enhance contextual understanding by referencing GIS documentation and tool-specific knowledge. The system generates structured workflows in JSON format, which are then executed through a Python-based geoprocessing engine capable of performing operations such as raster analysis, vector manipulation, terrain modeling, and suitability mapping. The results are visualized through an interactive Streamlit-based user interface that displays spatial outputs along with reasoning traces, improving user trust and interpretability. 

To demonstrate real-world applicability, the framework was evaluated on spatial decision-making tasks such as site suitability analysis and infrastructure planning, including identifying optimal locations for EV charging stations. These tasks typically require integrating multiple spatial datasets such as road networks, elevation models, land-use patterns, and proximity constraints. The system successfully automated the end-to-end workflow, from interpreting the natural language query to generating spatial maps that highlight suitable locations. Experimental results indicate that the generated workflows achieve high accuracy when compared to manually created GIS models, while significantly reducing development time and complexity. 

The key contribution of this project lies in combining AI-driven reasoning with geospatial data processing to create an explainable, automated, and scalable GIS workflow generation framework. Unlike traditional GIS automation tools that rely on predefined models or manual scripting, GeoSmartAI dynamically adapts to user intent and generates customized workflows for different spatial problems. The system promotes reproducibility, transparency, and efficiency, making it suitable for applications in urban planning, environmental monitoring, disaster management, and smart infrastructure development. 

In conclusion, GeoSmartAI demonstrates how Large Language Models can transform geospatial analysis by enabling natural language-driven spatial intelligence. The proposed framework represents a significant step toward the future of AI-assisted GIS, where complex spatial reasoning can be performed efficiently, transparently, and without requiring extensive technical expertise. Future enhancements may include real-time data integration, 3D spatial modeling, and cloud-based deployment to further improve scalability and performance.

D16ADA.title: ASTRA -Autonomous Security Threat Response Agent
D16ADA.description: Brute force attacks have been a major threat to network security, and traditional signature-based detection mechanisms have proven inefficient in detecting novel and variant attacks. Log analysis is both time-consuming and fallible, underlining the urgent demand for the use of intelligent, automated defense solutions. This paper proposes a novel intrusion detection solution called ASTRA (AI-based Brute Force Detection System with Confidence-Driven Autonomous Response and Action), a highly efficient intrusion detection framework that uses Isolation Forest for anomaly detection in combination with a response mechanism that relies on the concept of confidence. In contrast to traditional systems that are generally concerned only with detection, the proposed system assesses the level of confidence in the threats and automatically responds accordingly if the confidence level exceeds a predetermined threshold. The proposed system is validated on two datasets — CIC-IDS 2017 and CICIoT2023 — achieving 99.12% detection accuracy on brute-force attacks while demonstrating cross-dataset generalizability with SMOTE-augmented minority class handling. The results of our work prove that the proposed system fills the gap between detection and response mechanisms. Index Terms—Cybersecurity, Anomaly Detection, Machine Learning, Isolation Forest, Brute Force Attack, Autonomous Response, Intrusion Detection System, CIC-IDS 2017, CICIoT2023, SMOTE, SHAP Explainability

D16ADB.title: SurakshaNetra - A.I. Powered Stampede detection system
D16ADB.description:
Crowd stampedes are among the most critical safety hazards in large public gatherings, especially in high-density conditions where individual detection and tracking become unreliable. Effective early detection of such risks requires integrated modeling of crowd density, motion patterns, and their temporal evolution.

This paper presents a spatio-temporal graph-based representation of crowds derived from video surveillance data for proactive anomaly and stampede detection. Each video frame is processed using a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based density estimation model to generate a continuous crowd density map. The scene is then divided into fixed spatial regions, where each region is modeled as a graph node with associated density and motion features extracted using dense optical flow.

Spatial relationships between neighboring regions are represented through a grid-based graph structure, capturing local interactions within the crowd. Temporal dependencies are incorporated using a sliding window of consecutive graph instances, enabling the model to track evolving crowd behavior over time. This representation effectively captures key indicators such as crowd compression, motion intensity, and instability, along with their propagation across space and time.

The proposed structured framework provides a robust basis for both explainable anomaly detection and advanced learning-based spatio-temporal graph models. By combining spatial and temporal insights, the system enables early identification of potentially dangerous crowd conditions, allowing timely intervention.

Overall, this approach enhances the reliability of crowd monitoring systems and supports proactive management of high-density events, contributing to improved public safety and reduced risk of stampede incidents.

D16ADB.title: Dynamic Allocation of Spatial Spectrum for 6G using Agentic AI and RAG
D16ADB.description:
The transition towards sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks is expected to significantly increase the demand for spectrum resources due to the growth of high-bandwidth applications such as smart cities, real-time healthcare, and ultra-reliable low-latency communication. However, current spectrum management systems suffer from inefficient utilization due to static allocation mechanisms. In countries like India, this leads to congestion in urban areas while rural regions remain underutilized, widening the digital divide.
This project proposes a dynamic spectrum allocation framework using Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) combined with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The system employs a multi-agent architecture where specialized agents collaborate to make real-time decisions. These include a Master Orchestrator for coordination, a Policy Guardian to ensure compliance with regulatory standards, a Smart Allocator using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), a Fairness Agent based on Jain’s Fairness Index, and a Spectrum Monitor for continuous network analysis.
The model is trained on a large Pan-India dataset containing over 88,000 records with features such as bandwidth, frequency, power usage, and quality of service. A centralized training and decentralized execution approach using Advantage Actor-Critic enables efficient cooperation among agents. The system also incorporates priority factors such as disaster zones and critical infrastructure.
To improve transparency, a RAG module is integrated to generate human-readable explanations for every decision, addressing the limitations of black-box AI systems.
Experimental results show significant improvements, achieving 88.6% spectrum utilization, reduced latency of 7.9 ms, increased throughput of 10.2 Gbps, and a fairness index of 0.93. The system also ensures policy compliance and reduced energy consumption.

D16ADB.title:
EduAssist: An AI-Powered Teaching Assistant for
Academic Automation
D16ADB.description:
Faculty in higher education often spend a significant portion of their time on repetitive and administrative tasks such as preparing lecture materials, designing assessments, managing attendance, and maintaining academic records. These responsibilities reduce the time available for effective teaching, student interaction, and research activities. Although various digital tools exist to assist with individual tasks, they typically function in isolation and fail to provide a unified solution for end-to-end academic workflow automation.

This project presents *EduAssist*, an AI-powered teaching assistant designed to streamline and automate faculty workflows through an integrated, agent-based system. The platform leverages an agentic artificial intelligence framework, where multiple specialized agents collaborate to decompose complex academic tasks into manageable subtasks and execute them efficiently. By combining generative AI models with deterministic processing techniques, the system ensures both flexibility in content generation and structural reliability in outputs.

EduAssist incorporates a dual-model inference strategy, utilizing high-context reasoning models for structured academic generation and low-latency models for rapid drafting. This hybrid approach enables the automatic creation of syllabus-aligned instructional content, including lecture slides, quizzes, lab manuals, and academic documents. The system begins by converting unstructured syllabus documents into a structured format, which acts as the foundational knowledge base for all downstream operations. Natural language processing and rule-based validation mechanisms ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with institutional standards.

In addition to content generation, the platform automates academic administration processes such as attendance tracking, timetable management, and faculty record maintenance through a reliable, database-driven system. It also supports research-related activities by assisting in summarizing academic papers, drafting proposals, and organizing scholarly records. A human-in-the-loop design ensures that all generated outputs remain editable and under faculty control, maintaining accountability and trust.

The system follows a modular architecture consisting of request processing, agent orchestration, multi-model inference, validation, and output delivery. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy in syllabus parsing and substantial reductions in time required for academic tasks, with certain processes achieving significant efficiency improvements compared to manual methods.

Overall, EduAssist provides a comprehensive, scalable, and faculty-centric solution that enhances productivity, reduces workload, and enables educators to focus more on teaching and innovation.

D16ADB.title: KrishiMitra: Empowering Maharashtra  Agriculture Through AI
D16ADB.description:
KrishiMitra is an AI-powered, multi-agent agricultural decision-support system designed to provide region-specific and real-time guidance to farmers. Existing solutions are often fragmented and lack localization, ignoring key factors such as soil conditions, crop stage, and government policies.
To overcome this, KrishiMitra integrates specialized agents for crop planning, pest and disease advisory, and financial guidance, enabling a comprehensive approach to farming decisions. The system uses LoRA-based fine-tuning and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over verified government data to ensure accurate and reliable recommendations.
A central orchestration mechanism performs intent classification and context analysis, routing queries to the appropriate agents. With multilingual support and domain-specific knowledge bases, KrishiMitra delivers personalized, explainable, and policy-aligned insights, improving productivity and supporting sustainable agriculture.

D16ADB.title:
LLM-Powered Conversational AI for Stuttering
Detection and Therapy
D16ADB.description:
Stuttering affects approximately 1% of the global
adult population, yet access to speech therapy remains limited
due to high costs and therapist availability. Existing voice AI
systems are fundamentally incompatible with therapy needs as
they are trained to correct dysfluencies rather than detect them.
We present a hybrid neuro-symbolic architecture that combines
RMS-based signal processing for detecting physical struggle
patterns with Transformer-based ASR timestamp analysis for
linguistic dysfluencies. This detection engine is integrated into a
hierarchical agentic framework featuring a strategic planner that
generates personalized therapy curricula and a tactical session
manager that adapts exercise difficulty in real-time. Preliminary
evaluation on 412 speech samples achieves 89% accuracy. By
combining rule-based medical safety with LLM-driven person
alization, our system democratizes access to adaptive speech
therapy while maintaining clinical validity.

D16ADB.title: Legal Scenario Solver
D16ADB.description: Legal Scenario Solveris an AI-powered, multi-agent legal assistance system designed to provide accessible and real-time legal guidance to Indian citizens. Existing legal resources are often intimidating, filled with complex jargon, and lack clear procedural direction for the common person. To overcome this, Legal Scenario Solver integrates specialized agents for case intake, strategic advisory, IPC section identification, and automated document drafting, enabling a comprehensive approach to legal problem-solving. The system leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over verified Indian legal databases and penal codes to ensure accurate and grounded recommendations. A central orchestration mechanism performs intent classification and structured fact extraction, routing queries to the appropriate agents. With multilingual support and domain-specific knowledge bases, Legal Scenario Solver delivers personalized, explainable, and legally sound insights, improving legal literacy and simplifying the path to justice.

D16ADB.title: SmartServe: Agentic AI-Driven Hospitality Workforce Platform
D16ADB.description: The hospitality industry faces significant challenges in recruitment due to high employee turnover, seasonal demand fluctuations, and the need for rapid hiring decisions. Traditional recruitment methods rely heavily on manual resume screening and keyword-based Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), which are inefficient and unable to capture the contextual meaning of candidate skills and job requirements. As a result, these systems often produce inaccurate matches, overlook qualified candidates, and increase the workload for recruiters, ultimately affecting operational efficiency and service quality. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes SmartServe, an AI-powered semantic recruitment system designed specifically for the hospitality sector. The system leverages advanced Artificial Intelligence techniques such as Natural Language Processing (NLP), semantic embeddings, and multi-agent architecture to enhance recruitment accuracy and automation. SmartServe converts resumes and job descriptions into high-dimensional vector representations, enabling context-based matching using cosine similarity rather than simple keyword comparison. A hybrid scoring mechanism is implemented to further improve accuracy by incorporating domain-specific factors such as skills, certifications, experience, and shift availability. The system also utilizes a multi-agent framework where specialized agents handle tasks such as candidate matching, profile analysis, interview scheduling, and onboarding, allowing parallel processing and improved scalability. Additionally, a two-tier AI pipeline is employed, where lightweight models perform data extraction and advanced models handle reasoning and summarization, significantly reducing computational cost while maintaining performance. Experimental results demonstrate that SmartServe outperforms traditional recruitment systems, achieving higher matching accuracy, reducing time-to-hire, and lowering operational costs. The system improves Precision@10, enhances candidate relevance, and minimizes manual effort required by recruiters. Overall, SmartServe provides a scalable, efficient, and intelligent solution that transforms traditional recruitment processes into a faster, more accurate, and automated workflow. This approach not only improves hiring outcomes in the hospitality industry but also has the potential to be extended to other domains facing similar recruitment challenges.

D16ADB.title: TalentFlow AI : Next-Gen Resume Analysis
D16ADB.description:
TalentFlow is an AI-based talent management tool that is intended to assist, as opposed to replace,
human decision-making abilities. This manuscript discusses the basic concepts, complex algorithms,
and validation of the TalentFlow tool, with the aim of illustrating the potential of automation in the
optimization of the hiring process. It also explores the important issues in the global recruitment
industry, which is a $200 billion market with an average hiring process duration of 36 days, an
initial-year employee turnover rate of about 30%, and the causes attributed to the current hiring
process. The comprehensive analytics tool, which can process text, video, and other data modalities,
increases the accuracy of candidate-job fit while ensuring fairness across demographic
factors like age, gender, ethnicity, etc.

D16ADB.title: UPVEST - A smart and secure AI-driven platform
D16ADB.description: UpVest is a free AI-based financial literacy and investments platform designed for the young beginner investor, student, or professional from India to learn how to invest in stocks or mutual funds. The tool aims to solve major problems such as costly classes, generalized suggestions, the lack of real-life experience, and fragmentation by integrating education with tracking and managing of stock portfolios. Using the Google Gemini AI technology, the platform creates personalized 10-year investment plans based on personal financial profiles.These include factors like earnings, expenditures, and risk tolerance of a person.The educational process consists of video modules, live market updates from NIFTY 50 and SENSEX indexes, and gamification to apply theoretical knowledge in practice. In addition, you can link your Upstox DEMAT account for practical use.Developed using contemporary web development practices and APIs, the platform provides an immersive, interactive experience.Through the combination of technology, education, and investments, the UpVest platform helps young investors make confident and smart financial decisions.

D16ADB.title: Multimodal Ai Teaching Assistant
D16ADB.description:
In the rapidly evolving landscape of technical education, students often struggle to bridge the gap between theoretical coursework and practical implementation. Existing AI-based assistants typically provide generic responses that are not aligned with specific academic syllabi, limiting their effectiveness in structured learning environments.

This project presents MATA (Multimodal AI Teaching Assistant), a syllabus-aware, context-driven system designed to deliver personalized academic support for engineering students. The system leverages an Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, where multiple specialized agents—namely Learning, Lab, Research, and Project Assistants—collaborate to generate task-specific outputs.

The backend is implemented using FastAPI, with Mistral-7B as the core language model. Context retrieval is enabled through ChromaDB for vector storage, while LangChain is used to orchestrate multi-agent workflows. A key contribution of this work is a syllabus-ingestion pipeline, which processes course-specific PDF documents using semantic chunking techniques to ensure that responses remain strictly aligned with prescribed academic content.

MATA introduces a structured 4-stage Learning Flow, consisting of Explanation, Deep Dive, References, and MCQ-based evaluation. Additionally, the system includes an Interactive Lab Assistant capable of generating logic flow representations (via Mermaid diagrams) and viva preparation material. A Research and Project Advisor module integrates external scholarly APIs such as arXiv and Semantic Scholar to support academic exploration.

To enhance personalization, the system incorporates a Progress Tracking module, which analyzes user interactions to identify knowledge gaps and predict learning outcomes. By combining syllabus awareness, multi-agent collaboration, and adaptive learning strategies, MATA offers a scalable and intelligent alternative to conventional AI educational tools.

D16ADB.title: PCOS Management Network
D16ADB.description: This project proposes a multimodal AI-based system for early detection and management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) by integrating clinical data, ultrasonography image analysis, and patient interaction into a unified framework. The system uses a Random Forest classifier to analyze medical and biochemical data, while a CNN-based model detects ovarian follicles from ultrasound images, enhanced using techniques like CLAHE and bilateral filtering. Contour detection is applied for improved follicle identification. Additionally, a sentiment-aware chatbot provides personalized and empathetic health guidance to users. A retrieval-augmented generative AI module ensures accurate, context-based medical information by accessing a curated knowledge base, reducing misinformation. This integrated approach improves diagnostic accuracy, reduces delays caused by fragmented methods, and supports continuous patient care, making it a reliable and holistic solution for PCOS detection and long-term management.

D16ADB.title: WakalatAI : Law researcher using MCP Servers
D16ADB.description:
Legal research in the Indian judicial system involves processing large volumes of unstructured case laws, statutes, and precedents. Existing systems primarily rely on keyword-based retrieval, which fails to capture semantic relationships, contextual meaning, and user intent expressed in natural language. This results in inefficient workflows, irrelevant outputs, and increased manual effort in analyzing legal information. Additionally, the lack of transparency and structured reasoning in current systems limits their reliability for decision support.

Wakalat-AI is proposed as an AI-driven legal research framework that integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), agentic workflows, and modular system design to improve the efficiency and accuracy of legal information retrieval. The system accepts natural language case descriptions, which are processed through a query refinement stage involving entity extraction and semantic expansion, ensuring alignment with legal terminology.

The architecture is built using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which serves as an orchestration layer for managing communication between modular tools. The reasoning pipeline is implemented using LangGraph, enabling controlled, multi-step execution of tasks such as query expansion, document retrieval, legal analysis, and summary generation. Each step is structured as a node in a workflow, ensuring traceability and explainability. To maintain output consistency and reduce hallucinations, Pydantic is used for schema validation, enforcing structured responses including legal citations and entities.

The retrieval component uses a hybrid approach combining dense vector embeddings and external legal data sources. Legal documents are embedded into vector space, and cosine similarity is used to retrieve semantically relevant cases. This is complemented by external retrieval from platforms such as IndianKanoon, improving coverage. The retrieved data is then processed through the RAG pipeline, where the model synthesizes structured summaries, relevant precedents, and actionable insights.

The system also integrates domain-specific logic such as limitation period calculation, enhancing its practical utility. Experimental observations indicate improved retrieval relevance and reduced research time compared to traditional methods. Additionally, the structured reasoning workflow improves transparency and user trust.

In conclusion, Wakalat-AI presents a scalable and explainable approach to AI-assisted legal research. By combining MCP-based orchestration, LangGraph-driven reasoning, and Pydantic-based validation within a RAG framework, the system transforms unstructured legal data into structured, actionable insights, addressing key limitations of existing legal research tools.

D16ADB.title: Prompt Optimization and token efficiency in LLM for enterprise grade buisness
D16ADB.description:
As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly integrated into enterprise workflows, the cost and efficiency of prompt engineering have emerged as critical challenges. Organizations routinely spend significant computational resources on verbose, redundant, or poorly structured prompts that consume unnecessary tokens without improving output quality. This project presents Prompt Optimizer, a full-stack intelligent platform designed to automatically compress and optimize natural language prompts while preserving their semantic intent, logical structure, and contextual fidelity.

The system employs a multi-stage optimization pipeline that combines rule-based transformations with LLM-assisted refinement. In the first stage, a rule engine applies deterministic transformations — stripping polite padding, removing redundant qualifiers, eliminating filler phrases, and enforcing conciseness — to produce an initial compressed candidate. In subsequent stages, multiple optimization candidates are generated using configurable LLM adapters supporting providers such as Google Gemini and Hugging Face Inference API. Each candidate is then evaluated using a composite scoring function that weighs semantic similarity, token efficiency, readability, and logical preservation to select the optimal output.

A key innovation of the platform is its utility scoring engine, which balances token savings against meaning preservation using configurable weights (α for compression, β for semantic fidelity). This prevents over-compression — a common failure mode where aggressive shortening distorts the original intent. The system also incorporates a model routing service that dynamically selects the most appropriate LLM backend based on prompt complexity, budget constraints, and latency requirements, enabling cost-aware optimization across different organizational tiers.

The platform features a role-based access control (RBAC) system with distinct user roles — regular users, managers, and super admins — each with configurable token budgets and usage limits. An enterprise analytics dashboard provides real-time visibility into optimization performance, token savings, cost reduction, and usage trends across departments. A complete audit trail logs every optimization request, supporting compliance and accountability requirements.

The frontend is built with React and Vite, offering a responsive interface that includes an optimization workspace, history management with tagging and favorites, prompt evaluation scoring, model alternatives comparison, and an analytics dashboard with interactive charts. The backend is built on Node.js and Express, following a modular service-oriented architecture with middleware for authentication (JWT), rate limiting, request compression, and security hardening via Helmet.js.

Additional integrations include a Chrome extension for optimizing prompts directly from the browser, a VS Code extension for developer workflow integration, and a PowerShell CLI tool for terminal-based usage. Historical optimization data can be imported in bulk via CSV or JSON, enabling organizations to migrate existing prompt libraries and pre-populate analytics dashboards.

In evaluation, the system consistently achieves 20–35% token reduction across diverse prompt categories — including professional communication, technical documentation, creative writing, and customer support — while maintaining semantic similarity scores above 0.85. This translates directly to measurable cost savings for organizations consuming LLM APIs at scale.

The project demonstrates that intelligent prompt optimization, when implemented as a structured pipeline with semantic validation and adaptive scoring, can substantially reduce LLM operational costs without sacrificing output quality — making AI adoption more accessible and economically sustainable for enterprises of all sizes.

D16ADB.title: LungCareAI
D16ADB.description: Lung cancer continues to rank among the top malignant diseases responsible for cancer-related deaths globally. Therefore, the early and precise diagnosis of the disease is of critical importance for the betterment of patients. In this study, an explainable deep learning framework for multi-class classification of lung cancer using computed tomography images of the lungs, categorized as normal, benign, and malignant, is proposed. A comparative analysis of the proposed framework is carried out using pre-trained convolutional neural network architectures, namely ResNet50, VGG16, and DenseNet121. In addition to the classification performance of the proposed framework, this study also explores the concept of model explainability. In this study, the Grad-CAM technique is used for the visual representation of the discriminative regions of the images that affect the classification result. Furthermore, the concept of CAM Concentration Score (CCS) is proposed for the quantitative assessment of the concentration of the Grad-CAM technique. A comparative analysis of the proposed framework with the pre-trained models using CCS and entropy techniques indicates that different models with similar classification accuracy can have different spatial attention patterns.

D16ADB.title: VisionMate: AI based Digital Guide for Visually Impaired
D16ADB.description: Our system, VisionMate, is a real-time, AI-powered assistive framework designed to enhance independence and environmental awareness for visually impaired individuals. The system is orchestrated through a central agent-based architecture using LangGraph, which interprets user intent via voice input using Groq Whisper (whisper-large-v3) and dynamically routes tasks to specialized modules. The navigation pipeline combines a DeepLabV3 segmentation model and a fine-tuned YOLOv8-based obstacle detection model, trained on the Obstacles in Public Spaces for Dist-YOLO dataset (3350 images, 15 classes), along with MiDaS depth estimation to infer spatial distance and provide safe navigation cues. For scene understanding, a Vision-Language Model (LLaMA-4-based Groq Vision) is employed to generate contextual descriptions beyond object-level detection, enhancing environmental awareness.The text-reading module integrates OCR with VLM-based contextual reasoning, enabling robust handling of multilingual and complex visual text. A custom-trained YOLOv11 model, developed on an Indian currency dataset using Roboflow and deployed via ONNX runtime, supports real-time currency detection, ensuring low latency and offline capability. Additionally, system-level optimizations such as single-capture multi-frame processing and model preloading significantly reduce latency (e.g., reducing scene module latency from ~21s to ~3s), thereby improving real-time responsiveness. The final output is delivered to the user in audio form via Bluetooth using ElevenLabs speech synthesis integrated with Groq Whisper-based processing. Overall, VisionMate presents a scalable, efficient, and context-aware assistive solution that bridges the gap between perception, reasoning, and real-world usability for visually impaired users.

D16ADB.title: VikasYatra: AI-Powered Personalized Career Guidance
D16ADB.description:
VikasYatra (meaning “Journey of Progress”) is a full-stack, AI-powered educational technology platform designed to democratize personalized career guidance
through cutting-edge generative AI. The system integrates Google Vertex AI
(Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro), Imagen 4.0 image generation, Google Text
to-Speech (gTTS), OpenAI Whisper transcription, and Google Cloud
Translation API into a cohesive web application built with React 18 and
Flask (Python). The platform offers seven core intelligent modules: (1) a
conversational AI tutor with multi-modal voice support, (2) a doubt-solving
chatbot with session persistence, (3) an AI-powered quiz generator with adap
tive difficulty, (4) a personalized career roadmap engine producing directed
acyclic graphs, (5) a resume analyzer providing match scores against job descrip
tions, (6) a visual content generator converting text/PDF/audio to AI-narrated
videos, and (7) a multilingual translation service. The system employs Mon
goDB for persistent data storage, Firebase Authentication for secure user
management, and Cloudinary for cloud-based media asset management. This
report presents the system architecture, implementation methodology, AI model
configurations, performance metrics, and evaluation results demonstrating the
platform’s effectiveness in delivering personalized educational experiences.

D16ADB.title: Hybrid AI Interview Coach: An Adaptive Framework for Interview Training Using RAG and Real-Time Speech Processing
D16ADB.description: The fast pace of development in generative AI has completely changed the field of education technology, yet the realm of interviewing preparation software is largely comprised of static, text-driven tools ignoring the communicative value of oral communication. This paper highlights the limitations of existing interviewing practice approaches, such as preparing to answer questions from a bank and practicing alone, in creating the essential real-time feedback loop necessary to master speaking skills in technical environments. In response, a new hybrid interview coach is proposed, using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to adjust content according to resumes, while employing real-time Digital Signal Processing (DSP) technology for voice evaluation. Unlike the unpredictable autonomous generation agent, a hybrid model with adaptive behavior con trolled via state heuristics is used. The proposed hybrid system architecture consists of a React front-end interface, adaptive Flask back-end controller utilizing concept mastery velocity calculations, semantic duplicate filter, Sentence-BERT+FAISS RAG pipeline, Mistral API for generation, AssemblyAI for live transcript extraction, and YIN framework for estimating stream ing pitch stability, pause ratio, and WPM rate. This paper outlines architectural choices, algorithms, potential limitations, and possible future research directions in developing the system of multimodal interviewing coaching.
